title: USV own-ship navigation under GNSS spoofing: radar-to-chart fixes and an integrity monitor in the Oresund
summary: A simulated USV runs a 19.6 km transit over real geography (Lillgrund => Drogden channel => Copenhagen approach) built from OpenStreetMap coastline, Oresund bridge, wind turbines and seamarks, with 75 min of real Danish Maritime Authority AIS traffic as radar targets. Compass + bottom-track speed log dead reckoning, a 720-azimuth marine radar ray-cast with clutter, incidence-dependent detection and ship occlusion, likelihood-field + point-to-line ICP matching of returns to the chart (with degenerate, ambiguous and few-return checks), a 4-state EKF that also calibrates compass bias from matched heading, and a monitor (solution separation + 30 s GNSS-vs-radar/DR mean test, exclusion only when the GNSS-free filter has recent radar fixes). Over 5 seeds a slow GNSS drag (0.003 m/s^2 to 0.6 m/s) is excluded 125-131 s after onset near the coast at a 23-26 m offset (max error 10-25 m vs 1391-1395 m for GNSS+DR and for a single filter with radar but only innovation gates); onset in open water is caught at 202-250 s (max 71-102 m); a 1.5 km radar range makes it fail (175-1024 m). Zero false alarms in 25 runs. Writes navdash/1 JSONL for templates/demo-dashboard and own-ship CoT via the mavlink-to-tak-cot builder; README maps the pieces onto OpenCPN/radar_pi, Signal K, colav-simulator and MOOS-IvP.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06 on macOS with python 3.14.7 stdlib: 15 unit tests pass and three negative controls (detection off, degeneracy check off, isolation rule off) each make the targeted test fail; run.py for 5 scenarios x 4 configurations x 5 seeds, numbers in the README come from example_output/summary_5seeds.*; plot.py with matplotlib 3.11.2 (python 3.13.15); example_output/spoof-coastal loaded in templates/demo-dashboard in headless Chrome (metrics panel read). Fixtures built from Overpass (OSM) and a locally downloaded DMA AIS file for 2026-10-20. Not done: real radar data, S-57 ENC input, CoT in a TAK client, running any of the linked maritime stacks. Sensors, radar and attacks are simulated; the simulated world equals the OSM chart apart from buoy offsets, so radar fix errors are optimistic.
